seoTitle: How to Transfer Workspace Drive Files to Another Gmail
metaDescription: Move Google Drive files out of a Workspace account using the admin console or Google Takeout, and why the built-in ownership-transfer tool can never target a personal Gmail address.
intro: Leaving a job, closing a Workspace subscription, or consolidating accounts all raise the same problem: documents live inside a Google Workspace account that's about to go away. Google's admin console has a built-in tool for handing one user's Drive files to another user without re-uploading anything, but it only moves files between accounts inside the same Workspace organization. Google's own documentation states it can't transfer ownership to or from an external user, personal Google accounts included. This guide covers where that setting actually lives, what it can and can't do, and the two paths that do work for getting files into a personal Gmail account.
prerequisites: Admin access to the Workspace domain, specifically the Drive & Docs administrator privilege
For the direct transfer path: both the current and new owner must be accounts inside the same Workspace organization; a personal Gmail address doesn't qualify

steps.heading: Sign in to the Google Admin console
steps.body: Ownership transfer is an admin-level action, not something a regular Workspace user can do from their own Drive. Sign in at admin.google.com with an account that has admin rights on the Workspace domain the files currently live in. The admin home page gives you the full left-hand menu: Directory, Devices, Apps, Security, and more, which is also where billing and user management sit if this is part of shutting the account down entirely.

image.caption: The Google Admin console home screen. This is where the whole process starts; ownership transfer lives further inside the Apps section, not on this landing page.

steps.heading: Open Apps, then Google Workspace, then Drive and Docs
steps.body: From the left menu, drill into Apps and expand Google Workspace to see the individual services: Calendar, Gmail, Google Chat, Google Meet, and Drive and Docs among them. Click Drive and Docs, the settings hub for everything related to how Drive behaves across your organization, including sharing rules, migration settings, and the ownership tools needed here. It's easy to go looking for a "transfer" option under Users or Devices instead, so it's worth remembering the setting is filed under the app itself.

image.caption: The Google Workspace app list in the left menu, with Drive and Docs highlighted, the settings page you need is one click away.

steps.heading: Find Transfer ownership in the Drive and Docs settings
steps.body: The Drive and Docs settings page is organized as a stack of expandable sections: Google Apps Script, Migration Settings, Manage shared drives, and then Transfer ownership. Each one collapses to a single line describing what it does, so scroll until you see "Transfer ownership of one user's files to another user (useful when deleting a user)." That description is the giveaway that this feature was built for offboarding: moving a departing employee's files to a manager before their Workspace login is deactivated.

image.caption: The Drive and Docs settings page, showing Migration Settings, Manage shared drives, and Transfer ownership stacked as expandable sections.

steps.heading: Know the limit before you rely on this tool
steps.body: Expanding the Transfer ownership section confirms what it's built for: moving one user's files to another before that user's account is deleted, typically during offboarding. Google's documentation is explicit about the limit that matters here: transfers only work between accounts inside your organization, and "you can't transfer ownership to or from an external user, such as a personal Google Account or a user in another organization." That's a fixed rule, not a setting a domain administrator can switch on. If the destination is a personal Gmail address, this tool was never going to reach it, whatever else your domain's policies allow.

image.caption: The expanded Transfer ownership description, confirming it moves one user's files to another and is designed for use before deleting an account.

steps.heading: Use share-and-copy or Google Takeout instead
steps.body: For a personal Gmail destination, two paths work. Share the relevant folders with that Gmail address from the source Drive, then have the receiving account make its own copies; this creates a second copy instead of moving the original, but it preserves the content. For a full account's worth of data, Google Takeout is the better tool: it packages your Drive, or any subset of Workspace services you choose, into a downloadable archive to re-upload into the personal account. Takeout handles large volumes more reliably than sharing and copying dozens of items by hand, and it's the standard route when the whole Workspace account is closing rather than just changing who can reach a few files.

steps.heading: Confirm everything landed before the old account goes
steps.body: Open the personal Gmail account's Drive and check that folder structures, file counts, and anything specifically needed are all present before the Workspace account is deleted or deactivated. Google notes that a bulk transfer of an entire user's files, run ahead of deleting them, can take up to 36 hours to finish, and that certain items, Google Maps' own custom maps among them, don't transfer at all. Once the source account is gone, there's no route back to grab what didn't make it across.

troubleshooting.problem: Transfer ownership won't accept a personal Gmail address
troubleshooting.cause: This is a hard platform restriction: the admin console's ownership transfer only works between accounts in the same Workspace organization.
troubleshooting.fix: Use share-and-copy or Google Takeout instead. Neither depends on domain policy.

troubleshooting.problem: A bulk offboarding transfer is stuck or looks incomplete
troubleshooting.cause: Google states bulk transfers ahead of account deletion can take up to 36 hours, and files still in Trash or under litigation hold are skipped.
troubleshooting.fix: Empty Trash first, confirm there's no litigation hold on the account, and wait out the full window before assuming it failed.

troubleshooting.problem: Some files are missing from the personal account after a Takeout export
troubleshooting.cause: Certain file types, including Google Maps' own custom maps, aren't included in a Takeout export or a transfer.
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Takeout export summary against what's expected, and manually re-save anything unsupported before the source account closes.

faq.question: Can I transfer Drive files directly between a Workspace and personal Gmail account?
faq.answer: No. Google's admin console tool only moves files between accounts inside the same Workspace organization; it can't target or receive from a personal Gmail address, regardless of the domain's other settings. Share-and-copy or Google Takeout are the two paths that do reach a personal account.

faq.question: What is Google Takeout used for in this process?
faq.answer: Takeout exports Drive data as a downloadable archive, useful for transferring large volumes of files or wanting a full backup of an account rather than a selective ownership transfer.

faq.question: Will transferring files change their sharing permissions?
faq.answer: No. Google's documentation states that transferring ownership doesn't change who already has access to a file. What changes is who owns it, which matters for storage quota and for what survives after the original account is deleted.

faq.question: Why is the Transfer ownership option greyed out for me?
faq.answer: Most often because the signed-in account doesn't hold the Drive & Docs administrator privilege specifically. It also won't work at all if either account sits outside the Workspace organization; that's not something the setting itself can be switched to allow.

faq.question: Is there a size limit to how much I can transfer at once?
faq.answer: No published item-count or size limit for the ownership-transfer tool itself, but Google notes a bulk transfer of an entire user's files ahead of deleting their account can take up to 36 hours. Large Takeout exports are also better run in batches by service than as one export covering everything.
